label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, secret-rotation, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 6 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy webhook-receiver: WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION v2 -> v1); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: secret-rotation
case.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff.
case.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

expected_symptoms: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, the provider's webhooks not acknowledged, and the books rule fires at its second evaluation, about 50 s after the deploy
the receiver refuses every webhook with a 400, counts it as bad_signature and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'; the provider sends its growing backlog again and again, tens of times a second
nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka

payments and refunds still go through, but one whose answer was lost cannot be confirmed: its client's retries get 503 again, so the 5xx share of POST /payments about doubles and its p95 climbs to about 0.6 s, both under their thresholds

after the rollback the books catch up within about three minutes: the provider sends each refused webhook again within a minute of its last try, and one whose acknowledgement is then lost (the traffic's noise) a minute later
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, 133 of the provider's webhooks up to it had not been acknowledged yet.

diagnosis.hypothesis: webhook-receiver was redeployed at 21:20:02 with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. The provider still signs webhooks with the old secret, so the receiver now fails every signature check and answers 400 'webhook refused: bad signature'. Nothing is acknowledged or put on provider-events after that. The provider keeps resending, so the backlog of unacknowledged webhooks grows (133 at the alert, 21:20:50) and the money check cannot settle up to its cutoff. The total webhook rate is climbing because the same refused webhooks come back as retries, not because real traffic grew.

evidence.shows: webhook-receiver is the newest deploy, at 21:20:02, with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. That is 48 s before the alert. All other services were deployed at 21:18:36 and have not changed since.
Every recent webhook-receiver log line on /webhooks/provider is status 400 with 'webhook refused: bad signature', reason 'signature mismatch'.
Before 21:20 every webhook was 'queued'. 'bad_signature' first appears at 21:20:19 and climbs to about 19/s, while 'queued' falls toward zero by 21:20:34. The switch follows the deploy.
The total webhook rate rises from about 4/s to about 19/s after the deploy. This fits the provider resending refused webhooks.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to the settings it ran before the 21:20:02 deploy, which should be the previous secret version that matches the provider's signing key. The provider's retries should then be accepted and queued, and the backlog should drain. Afterwards, run money_check with wait=true to confirm the books caught up. If v2 is wanted, rotate it in coordination with the provider, or have the receiver accept both versions during the switch.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Only webhook-receiver is recreated, so it pauses briefly. Webhooks sent during the pause get no acknowledgement and the provider resends them, so nothing is lost. When the backlog drains, the consumers get a burst of events. ledger-consumer runs the idempotent handler and payment-confirmer looks events up by our id, so duplicate deliveries should not double-book. This is not verified here. Not checked: whether v2 was meant as a coordinated key rotation that the provider will switch to soon. If so, a rollback would only delay the rotation.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, for example if the provider has in fact moved to v2, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. Then check the logs and the klaxon_webhooks_received_total result label to see whether 'queued' or 'bad_signature' dominates.
